create.name: Caverly Morgan
create.bio:
Caverly Morgan began practising in 1995 and spent eight years in silent training at a Zen monastery before returning to ordinary life and starting to teach in 2001. Her teaching keeps the directness of Zen but is framed in nondual terms: she invites students to recognise that the peace they are looking for is already their own nature, using three simple supports she calls presence, inquiry and togetherness. She gives particular weight to what she calls relational dharma, treating relationships and community as a place of practice rather than a distraction from it.

She founded Peace in Schools, which created the first for-credit mindfulness course in American public high schools, and the nonprofit Realizing Freedom Together. Her book The Heart of Who We Are looks at how contemplative practice can serve collective as well as personal freedom, and she has also written a picture book on mindfulness for children. She leads a weekly livestreamed sit with discussion, online series, guided meditations on her YouTube channel, and residential retreats on Whidbey Island in Washington, where she lives, as well as elsewhere in the United States.

books.title: The Heart of Who We Are: Realizing Freedom Together
books.author: Caverly Morgan
books.description: Written after her years as a monk, the book asks how practices built for individual liberation can be turned towards shared problems. It mixes teaching, reflection and exercises on seeing through the sense of a separate self together.

books.title: A Kids Book About Mindfulness
books.author: Caverly Morgan
books.description: A short illustrated book for children that asks who they really are beneath their thoughts and feelings. It gives young readers and the adults reading with them simple ways to notice the present moment.

courses.title: The Body as a Gateway to Peace
courses.description: A residential retreat at the Whidbey Institute's forest land, taught with Davin Youngs, Jess Jarris and Sam Hammer. Days combine meditation, movement and sound, with the body used as a way into resting in awareness.

courses.title: Tuesday Morning Sit (livestream)
courses.description: A weekly online group with meditation followed by guided discussion on bringing awareness into daily life. Open to newcomers and experienced practitioners, offered on a sliding scale by donation.

courses.title: The Bridge to Happiness
courses.description: A self-paced online course hosted by Sangha Live. It starts from the view that our true nature is already whole and aware, and practises from there rather than from self-improvement.

courses.title: Awakening to the New Year: Navigating Chaos with Conscious Intention
courses.description: A four-module recorded course on Sangha Live about grounding in the present and setting intentions with care. First recorded for a new year, it can be taken at any time.

free_resources.title: Audio Library
free_resources.description: Free recorded talks and guided meditations, including pieces on resting in awareness and on the absolute and the relative, plus meditations suitable for teenagers.

free_resources.title: Video Library
free_resources.description: A free collection of her recorded talks and practices gathered on her website.

free_resources.title: Relational Dharma
free_resources.description: A free written teaching on practising within relationships, and on how our connections change once separation is seen through.
